title: Simson's Line: Closing the Converse via Complex Coordinates
content: Simson's theorem (published by William Wallace, 1797; named for Robert Simson) states that for a point P on the circumcircle of triangle ABC, the feet of the perpendiculars from P onto the three side-lines AB, BC, CA are collinear. The base development Proofs/SimsonLineTheorem.lean proves this forward direction (simson_key, simson_collinear). This file, imported on top of it, closes the genuinely new converse and upgrades the result to the full biconditional: the three pedal feet are collinear if and only if P lies on the circumcircle. The proof models points as complex numbers with the circumcircle normalised to the unit circle, so conj z = 1/z reduces the collinearity defect to a single polynomial identity. Zero axioms, zero sorries.
mathContext: On the unit circle, conjugation becomes inversion: $\bar z = 1/z$. The forward direction fixes $|p|=1$; the converse keeps $p$ free and shows the collinearity defect of the pedal feet equals a nonzero triangle factor times $(1-p\bar p)$, so it vanishes exactly when $p\bar p = |p|^2 = 1$.
prerequisites: conj z = z⁻¹ on the unit circle

title: Unit-Circle Helper Lemmas
content: Four private lemmas package the algebra of the unit circle used throughout. ne_zero_of_normSq_one: a point with normSq z = 1 is nonzero (needed before dividing by a, b, c). conj_eq_inv: on the unit circle conj z = z⁻¹, the substitution that turns conjugation into a rational operation. im_eq_zero_of_conj_eq and conj_eq_of_im_eq_zero: the two directions of the bridge conj z = z ⟺ z.im = 0, connecting the conjugate-equality collinearity criterion to the signed-area form.
mathContext: From $z\bar z = \operatorname{normSq} z = 1$ and $z\neq 0$ one gets $\bar z = z^{-1}$. A complex number is real iff it equals its conjugate iff its imaginary part is zero: $\bar z = z \iff \operatorname{Im} z = 0$.

title: The Collinearity Predicate FeetCollinear
content: def FeetCollinear a b c p packages the complex collinearity criterion for the three pedal feet F_AB = foot a b p, F_BC = foot b c p, F_CA = foot c a p: the cross product (F_BC − F_AB)·conj(F_CA − F_AB) equals its own conjugate, i.e. is real. This is exactly the conclusion of the base file's simson_key, exposed here as a reusable predicate over an arbitrary point p (no unit-circle hypothesis on p), so the converse can quantify over it.
mathContext: Three points $z_1,z_2,z_3$ are collinear iff $(z_2-z_1)\overline{(z_3-z_1)}\in\mathbb R$, i.e. $(z_2-z_1)\overline{(z_3-z_1)} = \overline{(z_2-z_1)}\,(z_3-z_1)$.

title: The Collinearity-Defect Identity (simson_defect)
content: simson_defect is the crux of the converse. With a, b, c on the unit circle but P arbitrary, the collinearity defect (F_BC − F_AB)·conj(F_CA − F_AB) − conj(F_BC − F_AB)·(F_CA − F_AB) collapses to the factored form (a − c)(c − b)(a − b)/(4abc)·(1 − p·conj p). This is the off-circle generalisation of the base file's simson_key. The proof rewrites the two foot differences with foot_diff/foot_diff', substitutes conj z = z⁻¹ for a, b, c via conj_eq_inv, and finishes with field_simp and ring.
mathContext: $(F_{BC}-F_{AB})\overline{(F_{CA}-F_{AB})} - \overline{(F_{BC}-F_{AB})}(F_{CA}-F_{AB}) = \dfrac{(a-c)(c-b)(a-b)}{4abc}\,(1-p\bar p).$ The left side is the collinearity defect; the right side factors the geometric content into a nonzero triangle prefactor times $1-|p|^2$.
prerequisites: conj z = z⁻¹ on the unit circle

title: The Biconditional (feet_collinear_iff)
content: feet_collinear_iff is the headline result: for a nondegenerate triangle (a ≠ b, b ≠ c, c ≠ a) with vertices on the unit circle, the three pedal feet are collinear ⟺ Complex.normSq p = 1, i.e. P lies on the circumcircle. The proof invokes simson_defect, shows the triangle prefactor (a−c)(c−b)(a−b)/(4abc) is nonzero (hK, via div_ne_zero and the pairwise distinctness), then uses mul_eq_zero so that the defect vanishes iff 1 − p·conj p = 0; Complex.mul_conj converts this to |p|² = 1 in both directions.
mathContext: Since the prefactor $K=\frac{(a-c)(c-b)(a-b)}{4abc}\neq 0$ for a nondegenerate triangle, the defect $K(1-p\bar p)=0 \iff 1-p\bar p = 0 \iff p\bar p = \operatorname{normSq}p = 1$. This is precisely 'P on the circumcircle'.

title: Signed-Area Form and Forward Direction
content: feet_collinear_iff_signed_area restates the predicate FeetCollinear as the vanishing of the signed area ((F_BC − F_AB)·conj(F_CA − F_AB)).im = 0, using the conj/im bridges — this is the form used by the base file's simson_collinear. simson_forward then recovers the classical forward direction of Simson's theorem (P on the circumcircle ⟹ feet collinear) as the trivial mpr half of the biconditional feet_collinear_iff.
mathContext: For $w=(F_{BC}-F_{AB})\overline{(F_{CA}-F_{AB})}$, the criterion $w=\bar w$ is equivalent to $\operatorname{Im} w = 0$ (twice the signed area of the pedal triangle). The forward direction is the immediate $\Leftarrow$ of the established $\iff$.
